correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts the two composite Omega<=2 shapes. For p^2, odd sigma(p^2) together with odd sigma(sigma(p^2)) forces sigma(p^2) to be a square, impossible between p^2 and (p+1)^2. For pq, p=2 contradicts abundancy monotonicity. For odd p,q, parity forces M=(p+1)(q+1) to be a square or twice a square. The exact abundancy inequalities exclude odd factors 3,5,7 from M and then all least primes below 37; the square-kernel divisibility and local abundancy inequality follow from even odd-prime valuations in M. Fresh exact arithmetic independently rechecked all small-prime abundance inequalities and the prime list; the finite verifier sweep is corroborative only.
residual_risks: The theorem is only a sieve: it does not exclude odd squarefree semiprime solutions with least prime at least 37.
